name: King of Tokyo
edition: Base game, original edition (rulebook ref. 51032, lot 09_2012A, copyright 2010-2012)

source.title: King of Tokyo instructions (2012), library-hosted copy

key_numbers.label: Cost to sweep the face-up cards

setup.text: Place the Tokyo board in the middle of the table. Nobody starts in Tokyo.

by_count.5: Use both Tokyo City and Tokyo Bay.
by_count.6: Use both Tokyo City and Tokyo Bay.

setup.text: Shuffle the power cards into a deck and turn the top 3 face up beside it.
Put the 6 black dice in the middle. Set the 2 green dice aside; only certain cards use them.
Make a pool of energy cubes and keep the counters beside the cards.
Choose a monster. Take its figure and board, then set life to 10 and victory points to 0.
Everyone rolls the 6 black dice. The most attack faces goes first. Play passes to the left.

turn.summary: Roll, resolve the dice, optionally buy cards, then end your turn.
steps: Roll all 6 dice, then reroll any or all of them, twice. You may keep or reroll dice again on the second reroll.
Resolve the final dice. Number faces score victory points, energy faces give energy cubes, heart faces heal, attack faces deal damage.
Triples of a number score that number in points, and each extra matching die adds 1.
Attack: from inside Tokyo, hit every monster outside it. From outside, hit every monster in Tokyo. Each damage costs 1 life.
If Tokyo is empty, the first monster to roll an attack takes it without dealing damage.
Buy any of the 3 face-up cards by paying energy, in any order and as often as you can afford. You may pay 2 energy to discard all 3 and reveal new ones.
Refill bought cards from the deck at once.
Resolve any end-of-turn effects, then pass the dice left.

end: The game ends when a monster reaches 20 victory points, or when only one monster is left alive. That monster wins.

scoring.text: Gain 1 point when you take control of Tokyo.
Gain 2 points when you start your turn in Tokyo.
Gain points from dice triples and from some cards.
A monster on 0 life is out of the game.

missed.text: A monster in Tokyo cannot heal with heart dice, but can heal with cards.
A monster attacked in Tokyo may yield its place to the attacker. It still takes the damage.
If an attack on Tokyo eliminates the monster there, the attacker takes control of Tokyo.
Damage from a discard card is not an attack, so nobody may yield Tokyo because of it.
Life cannot go above 10 unless a card says so.
You can reach 20 points and be eliminated in the same turn through cards; you must survive the turn to win.

With 5 or 6 monsters, an attacker outside Tokyo must take over Tokyo City first if it is empty or abandoned, then Tokyo Bay. A monster never holds both. If play drops below 5 monsters, the monster in Tokyo Bay must leave.

not_covered: The effects of individual power cards are not listed.
unverified: The exact number faces on the dice (1, 2 and 3) and the triple scoring are printed mostly as icons; they are inferred from the surrounding text and worked example.
